dispositions.rationale: Correct: exemption from the state cap is not exemption from every rent restriction, and local termination coverage is a separate question.
dispositions.change_applied: Replaced the 'no rent-increase cap at all' sentence with the reviewer's framing, added that affordability restrictions and recorded agreements still need checking, and separated Emeryville ordinance coverage (with the 30-day anti-evasion rule).
dispositions.quote_before: A unit that is exempt from AB 1482 has no rent-increase cap at all
dispositions.quote_after: An exempt unit is not subject to AB 1482's cap, but affordability restrictions, recorded agreements, and other applicable limits still need checking.

dispositions.rationale: Confirmed against eCode360 §5-40.06(b): failure to demonstrate service to the City does not invalidate the notice; §5-40.08 requires a notice in substantially the same form. 'City-required form' overstated it.
dispositions.change_applied: Quick Answer, step 3, consequences paragraph, checklist item, and video script (post 9215 and video page 9217) now say 'substantially the City's prescribed form' and carry the City-service exception while keeping the City filing mandatory.
dispositions.quote_before: Miss a precondition and the notice can be invalidated.
dispositions.quote_after: Miss most preconditions and the notice can be invalidated; the City filing is still mandatory, but failing to show City service alone does not invalidate the notice.

dispositions.rationale: Confirmed §5-40.02(e)(2): small landlord includes a landlord of a group residential facility of any size; unit count is covered units in Emeryville.
dispositions.change_applied: Updated Quick Answer, Key Facts row, relocation table, FAQ 5, and script (post and video page) to carry the full defined term.
dispositions.quote_before: Small landlord — 4 or fewer covered units
dispositions.quote_after: Small landlord — 4 or fewer covered units in Emeryville, or a group residential facility of any size

dispositions.rationale: Confirmed §5-40.02(j): the landlord must deliver an offer when conditions are met; written acceptance within 30 days; rent may not exceed the last month of the tenancy; survives change of ownership.
dispositions.change_applied: Replaced 'may be offered' with 'must offer' and kept the mailing-address, 30-day and written-acceptance conditions. Removed the Civil Code §827 parenthetical, which the ordinance text does not support.
dispositions.quote_before: the tenant may be offered it
dispositions.quote_after: the landlord must offer it back ... provided the tenant kept a current mailing address on file and delivers a written acceptance within 30 days of the offer

dispositions.rationale: Confirmed §5-40.02(b)(1): hotel/motel/short-term rental exemption applies only while occupancy does not exceed 30 consecutive days, with an anti-evasion rule.
dispositions.change_applied: Qualified the exemption in the coverage paragraph and FAQ 3; replaced broad statements with 'covered tenancy' in Key Facts, body, and script. Replaced the unverified 'two or fewer bedrooms' owner-occupied wording with 'certain owner-occupied residences'.
dispositions.quote_after: hotels, motels and short-term rentals where the tenant does not reside more than 30 consecutive days

dispositions.rationale: Reviewer's point is right: mailed service adds time under CCP §1013 and a longer governing notice requirement controls.
dispositions.change_applied: Added the mailing and longer-notice caveat to the body paragraph and the checklist item. CCP §1013 and Civil Code §827(b)-(c) were taken from the review and not independently re-fetched this round.
dispositions.quote_before: generally 30 days if it totals 10% or less, 90 days if more (Civil Code §827(b)).
dispositions.quote_after: ... (Civil Code §827(b)). If the notice is served by mail, additional time applies under Code of Civil Procedure §1013, and any longer notice requirement that governs your tenancy controls.
